doc.title: David Friesen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2024

chapter: Playing and listening in the moment
title: Listening, audience awareness, and writing at the piano
summary: He trains himself to listen and respond; he only considers the audience afterward, and tells of a film crew he failed to notice while writing at the piano.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: almost separately about what is my audience hearing. Do I want to play in a manner that I’m cognizant of what people in the audience are hearing.

The only time, of course when I’m playing my mind, my ears, my whole soul is, I’ve trained myself to listen and respond creatively to what I’m hearing. That’s my — I have it in my little book I wrote “listening is my life preserver in the ocean of sound, without it I drown.” And so I’m continually doing that. The times I do think about the audience is if I have a composition and I play it and now — if there’s an audience — I’ve played where there’s been no audience. But this is when there is an audience I can hear how they respond. I listen to how they respond to the piece that’s just been played. And I can think, “Oh yeah, they liked this one, uh huh, well I’m going to use this one on the next gig and I’ll see how they respond to that.” But that’s when I’ll think about the audience. But I never think about — I don’t have time to think about them when I’m — like today I was at the piano playing and I suddenly realized that we were going to be doing the interview so I went and looked — no I’m four minutes late. I get involved with what I’m doing. And I had a film crew come to my house once. They were doing a segment on local television about artists. And they said, “No David, just go ahead and do what you’re doing and we’ll take care of everything.” And I was at the piano writing a new tune and after a while I felt someone tap me on the shoulder and said, “Hello, David.” And I looked and I was kind of surprised there were people there but then I remembered, you know. I’ve trained myself.

I think I might have heard of that. Did that person — I think you told that person, if it was the same video, that you sort of get a message that there’s a song waiting for you at the piano. Just go there and — yeah.
I wish someone would tell me to do that.
Oh you play sax — do you play tenor or alto?
I play alto mostly but I also play the piano so usually I write at the piano and see what’s —
Yeah, well all the harmony is right there, so. I can call you up and tell you go to the piano if you like.
